Prediction Object for Competing Risks

Source: R/PredictionCompRisks.R
PredictionCompRisks.Rd

Stores competing risks predictions returned by a learner of class LearnerCompRisks.

  • The $cif field provides cumulative incidence function (CIF) predictions, with one matrix (observations x times) per cause.

  • The $times field provides the corresponding numeric time grids (can be different per cause).

  • The $cause_names field provides the descriptive cause names.

  • The $raw field provides optional upstream predictions, such as cause-specific hazard matrices.

  • The task_type is set to "cmprsk".

Raw predictions

A learner can provide alternative upstream predictions, such as all-cause survival estimates or cause-specific hazard matrices, in the raw element of the list returned by its .predict() method. Set learner$predict_raw = TRUE to request these values from a learner that supports them. Keep in mind that:

  • Filtering prediction rows via $filter() retains the entire raw object.

  • Combining multiple predictions via c() collects the non-NULL raw objects into a list in input order and each object is kept intact. The combined $raw is NULL if none of the inputs supplies a raw object.

  • as.data.table() omits raw predictions completely. Access them directly through $raw.

Super class

mlr3::Prediction -> PredictionCompRisks

Active bindings

times

(list())
Read-only numeric time grids, named by cause code and stored as an attribute of $data.

cause_names

(character())
Read-only descriptive cause names, named by cause code and stored in the attribute states of $truth.

cif

(list())
Read-only list of CIF matrices with column names derived from the corresponding $times vectors.

PredictionCompRisks$new()

Creates a new instance of this R6 class.

Usage

PredictionCompRisks$new(
  task = NULL,
  row_ids = task$row_ids,
  truth = task$truth(),
  cif,
  times,
  weights = NULL,
  check = TRUE,
  extra = NULL,
  raw = NULL
)

Arguments

task

(TaskCompRisks)
Task, used to extract defaults for row_ids and truth.

row_ids

(integer())
Row ids of the predicted observations, i.e. the row ids of the test set.

truth

(survival::Surv())
True observed response. Descriptive cause names are derived from the states attribute, ordered by numeric cause code.

cif

(list())
A required list of two or more matrix objects. Each matrix represents a different competing event (or cause) and stores the cumulative incidence function (CIF) for each test observation. For each matrix, rows refer to observations and columns to time points. CIF lists must use numeric cause codes as names, i.e. "1", "2", ..., "K", exactly in that order.

times

(list())
Named list of numeric time vectors, with the same names and order as the CIF list. Time points must be finite, unique, non-negative, strictly increasing numbers, and have one entry per corresponding CIF matrix column. Different causes may use different time grids.

weights

(numeric())
Optional measurement weights for the predicted observations, as supplied by a task with column role "weights_measure".

check

(logical(1))
If TRUE (default), performs argument checks which is encouraged for user-supplied data. With FALSE, inputs are assumed valid and correct behavior is not guaranteed.

extra

(list())
Optional named list of additional per-observation data. Each element must have the same length as row_ids. Names must not be row_ids, time, event, CIF, or weights, which are reserved prediction columns.

raw

(any)
Optional upstream predictions or metadata, such as a vector, matrix, or list. The constructor stores the object as-is without validation.

Details

The cif input is a named list of numeric CIF matrices, with rows = observations and columns = time points. The list names are consecutive cause codes ("1", "2", ..., "K") matching the task's competing events/causes. The times argument is required and supplies the corresponding time grid for each cause. Predictions contain a matrix for every task cause, including causes absent from the observed response of the predicted observations. Filtering observations retains all causes and their CIF matrices. Combining predictions requires matching cause codes and descriptive names, and aligns each cause's matrices on the union of its time grids.

With check = TRUE, nonempty predictions are validated using assert_cif_list(). This checks the list structure and cause codes, the time points used for prediction, and validates that each CIF matrix includes probabilities in [0, 1] which are non-decreasing over time.

With options(mlr3cmprsk.warn_cif_sum = TRUE), joint coherence is checked separately by aligning the CIF matrices on a common time grid and summing their probabilities across causes for each observation and time point. A sum greater than 1, allowing a numerical tolerance of sqrt(.Machine$double.eps), triggers a warning of class Mlr3WarningCIFSumExceedsOne. This diagnostic is disabled by default; see the Package Options section in mlr3cmprsk-package. Predictions are retained without modification. Such violations can arise when cause-specific CIFs are estimated independently, as with separately fitted Fine-Gray subdistribution hazards models.

PredictionCompRisks$clone()

The objects of this class are cloneable with this method.

Usage

PredictionCompRisks$clone(deep = FALSE)

Arguments

deep

Whether to make a deep clone.

Examples

library(mlr3)
task = tsk("pbc")
task$select(c("age", "chol", "albumin", "ast", "bili", "protime"))
learner = lrn("cmprsk.fg")
part = partition(task)
p = learner$train(task, part$train)$predict(task, part$test)
p
#> 
#> ── <PredictionCompRisks> for 91 observations: ──────────────────────────────────
#>  row_ids time event       CIF

#>        6 1832     0 <list[2]>
#>       18 1356     2 <list[2]>
#>      ---  ---   ---       ---
#>      266 1271     0 <list[2]>
#>      274  939     0 <list[2]>
#>      276  788     0 <list[2]>

# CIF list: one matrix (obs x times) per competing event
str(p$cif)

# example raw predictions
# attach random cause-specific hazard matrices
n_obs = length(p$row_ids)
cs_hazard = lapply(p$times, function(cause_times) {
  matrix(runif(n_obs * length(cause_times)), nrow = n_obs)
})

p_raw = PredictionCompRisks$new(
  row_ids = p$row_ids,
  truth = p$truth,
  cif = p$cif,
  times = p$times,
  raw = list(cs_hazard = cs_hazard)
)
str(p_raw$raw$cs_hazard)
#> List of 2
#>  $ 1: num [1:91, 1:12] 0.7298 0.0384 0.3338 0.7493 0.9132 ...
